findings.issue_text: Migration in db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb inserts legacy setting values raw without scheme/path stripping, so previously-working embed hosts fail host_allowed? and embedding returns InvalidAccess after upgrade
app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update/destroy with a nonexistent or already-deleted id crashes with NoMethodError on nil, returning a 500 instead of a 404/4xx

app/models/embeddable_host.rb validation regex allows port-bearing hosts like eviltrout.com:8080, but record_for_host compares against uri.host which excludes the port, so such hosts can never match and embedding is permanently denied

The diff adds admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6 and registers 'embeddable-host' in ADMIN_MODELS but defines no Ember model for either type, so createRecord/find resolve to undefined and the entire /admin/customize/embedding page fails to render

app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-41 — embed_category site setting is deleted and its replacement eh.try(:category_id) yields nil for feed-polled import URLs with no matching host row, so imported topics lose their configured category with no fallback

spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contents are swapped — category_fabricator.rb contains the embeddable_host fabricator and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contains the category fabricators, a comprehension hazard

spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and embedding_controller_spec.rb provide only class-hierarchy assertions with zero coverage of create/update/destroy behavior, validation failures, nil-record paths, category_id fallback, or the data-transforming migration
EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that re-renders fetch_embedding, and the client saveChanges() calling update({}) is dead code never invoked from any template

store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded's plural branch does not filter undefined entries, so a side-loaded payload missing an id yields colors: [undefined], and template iteration over the hasMany throws on property access

spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1402-1404 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what it claims since expandable_first_post? no longer reads hosts; it passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, misleading future debuggers

The entire embedding-update path is a no-op that reports success: EmbeddingController#update renders the show payload and persists nothing, client saveChanges() calls update({}), and the template never wires saveChanges to a button — an API client PUTting /admin/customize/embedding gets a 200 while nothing changed; the route, update action, and saveChanges action should be deleted

category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contents are swapped: embeddable_host fabricator lives in category_fabricator.rb and the category fabricators live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — file names should match their contents

EmbeddableHost validation regex permits an optional port (:[0-9]{1,5}) so admins can save example.com:8080, but record_for_host matches uri.host (port stripped) against lower(host) = ?, so hosts with ports silently never allow embedding; either reject ports in the regex or compare host+port

Behavior regression: the old site-setting path accepted TLD-less hosts like localhost or intranet names, but the new format regex requires a .[a-z]{2,5} TLD, so installations upgrading from settings containing such hosts lose embedding and cannot re-enter the same value through the new UI

Migration 20150818190757 interpolates the raw legacy embeddable_hosts setting value directly into SQL, so a stored value containing a single quote aborts the migration mid-execution; use EmbeddableHost.new(...).save(validate: false) or quote the literal
topic_spec.rb removes the unused 'topic =' local in two for_digest tests — unrelated drive-by churn in a feature PR that inflates the diff a reviewer must audit

store-test.js.es6 only converts two tests to the assert.* style while the rest of the file still uses the global ok/equal style, leaving two conventions in one file; convert the whole file or keep touched tests in the existing style

EmbeddableHostSerializer re-declares id, host, and category_id attribute methods that exactly duplicate ApplicationSerializer's default attribute serialization — 13 lines of dead code that can be deleted with zero behavior change

EmbeddableHostsController#update/#destroy fetch EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no nil check, so a stale or bogus id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404 — e.g. an admin with two embedding tabs open hits a 500 after deleting a host in the other tab

Write path and lookup path disagree on canonical form for ports: validation permits and persists a port (example.com:8080), but record_for_host uses URI#host which never contains a port, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? always returns false for hosts with ports

record_for_host lowercases the stored host column but not the lookup parameter, so a referer with uppercase letters (e.g. EvilTrout.com) never matches a stored lowercase row, causing host_allowed? to return false for allowed hosts (also affects TopicEmbed.import fallback to no category)

Migration raw INSERT bypasses the model's normalization, migrating setting entries with schemes (e.g. http://example.com) into rows that record_for_host can never match, silently breaking previously working embeds after upgrade
No UNIQUE constraint on host column and record_for_host uses .first with no ORDER BY, so duplicate host rows yield nondeterministic category assignment for imported topics

Admin embeddable_hosts controller update/destroy actions lack a nil check on EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, causing NoMethodError and a 500 response when the id is missing or deleted concurrently
No foreign key on category_id, leaving dangling category references after category deletion which breaks category badges and causes embed imports to fail
No index on host column, so the lower(host) lookup runs unindexed on every embed request (hot path)

Migration crashes with NoMethodError on sites that never customized embed_category: the category lookup calls [0]['id'] unguarded, and since site_settings only stores non-default values, the join returns zero rows and nil['id'] raises, aborting db:migrate

No cleanup of embeddable_hosts rows when a category is deleted, so record_for_host keeps returning records whose category_id points at a destroyed category, causing broken or silently recategorized embedded topics in TopicEmbed.import

Topic#expandable_first_post? silently dropped its 'hosts configured' guard: the new condition SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed? expands first posts even when all embeddable hosts have been deleted, an unconfirmed behavior change

SQL injection risk in migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb: host values from the embeddable_hosts site setting are interpolated directly into an execute INSERT statement with no escaping or parameter binding; a stored host containing a single quote can break the SQL literal, fail the migration, or execute injected SQL (P2)

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb update/destroy with a nonexistent or already-deleted id crashes with NoMethodError on nil, returning a 500 instead of a 404/4xx

app/models/embeddable_host.rb never normalizes host case, but record_for_host compares lower(host) against an un-downcased referer host, so mixed-case stored hosts never match and embedding is silently denied

app/models/embeddable_host.rb validation regex allows port-bearing hosts like eviltrout.com:8080, but record_for_host compares against uri.host which excludes the port, so such hosts can never match and embedding is permanently denied

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the validation regex explicitly allows an optional port (e.g. ":8080"), and the before_validation hook strips scheme and path but does not remove a port, so a saved record can be "eviltrout.com:8080". However record_for_host(host) parses the URL and then compares only uri.host (which excludes the port) via where("lower(host) = ?", host). Therefore a stored host that includes a port can never be matched/allowed, causing EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer) to deny embedding for that configuration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The diff adds admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6 and registers 'embeddable-host' in ADMIN_MODELS but defines no Ember model for either type, so createRecord/find resolve to undefined and the entire /admin/customize/embedding page fails to render

adjudication.rationale: While the diff indeed adds an admin adapter for `embedding` and uses `this.store.find('embedding')` / `this.store.createRecord('embeddable-host')` without adding any new `app/assets/javascripts/**/models/{embedding,embeddable-host}.js.es6` files in this patch, the finding’s conclusion that these calls “resolve to undefined” and that the admin embedding page “fails to render” is not verifiable from the diff. This codebase uses a custom `discourse/models/store` + `discourse/adapters/rest` (not Ember Data), where types can be handled via generic REST model behavior and adapters without requiring explicit per-type model classes. The diff alone doesn’t demonstrate a runtime error or missing lookup behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:36-41 — embed_category site setting is deleted and its replacement eh.try(:category_id) yields nil for feed-polled import URLs with no matching host row, so imported topics lose their configured category with no fallback

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the global `embed_category` setting (site_settings.yml and locales) and changes `TopicEmbed.import` to set `category: eh.try(:category_id)` after `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). There is no explicit fallback category in `TopicEmbed.import` if `eh` is nil. However, the diff also changes host validation for embedding/retrieval to rely on `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` (e.g., lib/topic_retriever.rb and embed_controller.rb), which suggests callers should only reach import for allowed hosts. Because the diff doesn’t show the feed-polling/import call path and whether it can invoke `TopicEmbed.import` without first ensuring a matching `EmbeddableHost`, the claimed broken behavior for “feed-polled import URLs with no matching host row” isn’t fully verifiable as an actual defect from this diff alone, but the missing fallback/guard is a concrete edge-case concern introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and embedding_controller_spec.rb provide only class-hierarchy assertions with zero coverage of create/update/destroy behavior, validation failures, nil-record paths, category_id fallback, or the data-transforming migration

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial behavior in `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` (create/update/destroy paths via `save_host`, params handling, `category_id` fallback to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`, and error rendering on `host.save` failure) and `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb` (show/update with `fetch_embedding`). However, the new specs `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` only assert the controllers subclass `Admin::AdminController` and do not exercise any of the new actions/edge cases mentioned. The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` also performs data transformation (reading old `site_settings`, inserting records, deleting settings) without any test coverage. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap rather than a proven runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddingController#update is a no-op that re-renders fetch_embedding, and the client saveChanges() calling update({}) is dead code never invoked from any template

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not persist any changes (it just re-renders the serialized `@embedding` fetched in `before_filter :fetch_embedding`), making it effectively a no-op. On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})`, but `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` never invokes `saveChanges` (only `addHost` and `deleteHost` are wired, and per-host saving happens via `host.save` in the `embeddable-host` component). This is verifiable dead/unused functionality but not a user-visible defect given hosts are managed through `/admin/embeddable_hosts`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6 _hydrateEmbedded's plural branch does not filter undefined entries, so a side-loaded payload missing an id yields colors: [undefined], and template iteration over the hasMany throws on property access

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural `_ids` branch (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`) maps each id via `_lookupSubType` but never filters out falsy results: `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => self._lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` while always `delete obj[k]`. If a side-loaded payload contains an id that cannot be looked up (missing from `root`), `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined`, producing arrays like `[undefined]` and removing the original `*_ids` field, which can break downstream iteration/property access. The singular branch explicitly guards with `if (hydrated)` and does not delete the key when missing, highlighting the inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1402-1404 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what it claims since expandable_first_post? no longer reads hosts; it passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false, misleading future debuggers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` to no longer consult any embeddable-host setting (`topic.rb`: now only `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the example still says "is false if embeddable_host is blank" but it doesn't set `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` to true or stub `has_topic_embed?`, so it will pass simply because `embed_truncate` defaults to false (per `config/site_settings.yml`). That makes the test assertion/description misleading and no longer testing what it claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The entire embedding-update path is a no-op that reports success: EmbeddingController#update renders the show payload and persists nothing, client saveChanges() calls update({}), and the template never wires saveChanges to a button — an API client PUTting /admin/customize/embedding gets a 200 while nothing changed; the route, update action, and saveChanges action should be deleted

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a PUT route `/admin/customize/embedding` mapped to `Admin::EmbeddingController#update`, but `#update` only re-renders the serialized `@embedding` and performs no persistence or mutation (it’s identical to `#show`). On the client, `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` defines `saveChanges()` as `this.get('embedding').update({});` (an empty update), and `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` provides no UI control that triggers `saveChanges` (only `addHost`). Thus a PUT to the new endpoint will return 200/success JSON while changing nothing, which is broken/misleading behavior introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: category_fabricator.rb and embeddable_host_fabricator.rb contents are swapped: embeddable_host fabricator lives in category_fabricator.rb and the category fabricators live in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — file names should match their contents

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the fabricator definitions moved in a way that makes filenames not match their contents: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now contains the `Fabricator(:category)` (and related category variants). This is verifiable from the diff and is a maintainability/convention issue; it may not break tests if all fabricators are auto-loaded, but it’s still a concrete review concern grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHost validation regex permits an optional port (:[0-9]{1,5}) so admins can save example.com:8080, but record_for_host matches uri.host (port stripped) against lower(host) = ?, so hosts with ports silently never allow embedding; either reject ports in the regex or compare host+port

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost` the validation regex explicitly allows an optional port `(:[0-9]{1,5})?` (and `before_validation` strips scheme/path but not the port), so a saved `host` value like `example.com:8080` is permitted and will be stored. However `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL and compares only `uri.host` (port-stripped) via `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`, so `example.com` will never match a stored `example.com:8080`, causing such entries to silently never allow embedding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavior regression: the old site-setting path accepted TLD-less hosts like localhost or intranet names, but the new format regex requires a .[a-z]{2,5} TLD, so installations upgrading from settings containing such hosts lose embedding and cannot re-enter the same value through the new UI

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model adds `validates_format_of :host` with a regex requiring a dotted hostname and a 2–5 letter TLD (`...*\.[a-z]{2,5}...`), so values like `localhost` or intranet single-label hosts will fail validation and cannot be (re)entered/saved via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` (which calls `host.save`). The removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` logic did not impose this dotted/TLD requirement (it parsed via `URI(host).host` and compared strings), so this is a real regression in what hosts can be configured. The claim that upgrades "lose embedding" depends on existing data/migration behavior, but the inability to save TLD-less hosts through the new system is directly introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration 20150818190757 interpolates the raw legacy embeddable_hosts setting value directly into SQL, so a stored value containing a single quote aborts the migration mid-execution; use EmbeddableHost.new(...).save(validate: false) or quote the literal

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, legacy host strings from the site_settings table are interpolated directly into a raw SQL INSERT: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`. If any stored embeddable_hosts line contains a single quote (or other SQL-significant characters), the generated SQL becomes invalid and the migration can fail mid-run (and also risks unintended SQL execution). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_spec.rb removes the unused 'topic =' local in two for_digest tests — unrelated drive-by churn in a feature PR that inflates the diff a reviewer must audit

adjudication.rationale: In spec/models/topic_spec.rb, two for_digest tests change `topic = Fabricate(...)` to just `Fabricate(...)` (the local was unused). This is unrelated cleanup within an embedding-feature PR and increases diff surface area reviewers must scan, though it doesn't introduce a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store-test.js.es6 only converts two tests to the assert.* style while the rest of the file still uses the global ok/equal style, leaving two conventions in one file; convert the whole file or keep touched tests in the existing style

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows only two tests in store-test.js.es6 being updated to take an `assert` parameter and use `assert.ok/assert.equal`. Whether the rest of the file still uses global `ok/equal` isn’t verifiable from the provided diff context, and in any case this is a style/convention concern rather than a concrete defect or substantive review issue grounded in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostSerializer re-declares id, host, and category_id attribute methods that exactly duplicate ApplicationSerializer's default attribute serialization — 13 lines of dead code that can be deleted with zero behavior change

adjudication.rationale: In EmbeddableHostSerializer, the methods `id`, `host`, and `category_id` simply return `object.id/host/category_id` while the serializer also declares `attributes :id, :host, :category_id`. This is at most a minor redundancy/cleanup suggestion, not a verifiable defect. The claim that deleting them causes “zero behavior change” depends on ApplicationSerializer’s behavior, which is not shown in the diff, so it can’t be strictly verified here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EmbeddableHostsController#update/#destroy fetch EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no nil check, so a stale or bogus id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404 — e.g. an admin with two embedding tabs open hits a 500 after deleting a host in the other tab
matched_golden_ids: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that update/destroy retrieve EmbeddableHost via `where(...).first` without checking for nil, leading to a NoMethodError (500) when the ID is invalid or the record was deleted—same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Write path and lookup path disagree on canonical form for ports: validation permits and persists a port (example.com:8080), but record_for_host uses URI#host which never contains a port, so EmbeddableHost.host_allowed? always returns false for hosts with ports

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the `host` field validation regex explicitly allows an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), and `before_validation` strips scheme and path but does not strip the port, so records can be saved as e.g. `example.com:8080`. However, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL via `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host`, which never includes the port, and then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. That lookup will not match stored values containing `:port`, causing `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` to return false for port-qualified hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: record_for_host lowercases the stored host column but not the lookup parameter, so a referer with uppercase letters (e.g. EvilTrout.com) never matches a stored lowercase row, causing host_allowed? to return false for allowed hosts (also affects TopicEmbed.import fallback to no category)
matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: record_for_host uses a case-insensitive comparison on the stored host (lower(host)) but fails to normalize/lowercase the input parameter, so mixed/upper-case referer hosts won’t match even when they should.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration raw INSERT bypasses the model's normalization, migrating setting entries with schemes (e.g. http://example.com) into rows that record_for_host can never match, silently breaking previously working embeds after upgrade

adjudication.rationale: In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, existing `site_settings.embeddable_hosts` lines are migrated via raw SQL: `INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, which bypasses `EmbeddableHost`'s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. Later, `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` parses the URL and matches with `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`, so rows stored as `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` will not match `discourse.org` / `example.com`, breaking previously-allowed embeds after upgrade. The diff’s updated tests explicitly show prior settings could include schemes/paths (e.g. `Fabricate(:embeddable_host, host: 'http://discourse.org')`, `host: 'https://example.com/1234'`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No UNIQUE constraint on host column and record_for_host uses .first with no ORDER BY, so duplicate host rows yield nondeterministic category assignment for imported topics

adjudication.rationale: The migration creates `embeddable_hosts(host, category_id, ...)` with no UNIQUE index/constraint on `host` (and the model also lacks a `validates_uniqueness_of :host`). `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` without `ORDER BY`, so if duplicate rows exist the chosen record (and thus `category_id` used in `TopicEmbed.import` via `eh.try(:category_id)`) is nondeterministic. The admin controller allows creating hosts without any duplicate check, so this ambiguous state is reachable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embeddable_hosts controller update/destroy actions lack a nil check on EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first, causing NoMethodError and a 500 response when the id is missing or deleted concurrently

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch with `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` but do not handle the not-found case. `update` then calls `save_host(host)` which dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`, `host.category_id = ...`), and `destroy` calls `host.destroy`. If the record is missing (invalid id or concurrently deleted), this will raise `NoMethodError` on nil and result in a 500 response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No foreign key on category_id, leaving dangling category references after category deletion which breaks category badges and causes embed imports to fail

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `embeddable_hosts.category_id` (migration `create_embeddable_hosts` sets it `null: false`) and uses it throughout (UI renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`, server import uses `eh.try(:category_id)` in `TopicEmbed.import`). However, the diff does not add any DB-level foreign key or application-level cleanup/guard for when a Category is deleted (no `dependent:`/callback, no reassignment to uncategorized on category deletion). That makes dangling `category_id` references possible. The finding’s specific claim that this *will* break badges/imports depends on how category deletion is handled elsewhere (not shown), so the concrete failure is not fully verifiable from the diff alone, but the integrity gap itself is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No index on host column, so the lower(host) lookup runs unindexed on every embed request (hot path)

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` creates `embeddable_hosts` with `t.string :host, null: false` but adds no index on `host` (or on `lower(host)`). The lookup used on the embed hot path is `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` which executes `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, so without a functional index (or alternative downcased storage + index) this will likely require a sequential scan as the table grows. This is a performance/operability issue rather than a correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration crashes with NoMethodError on sites that never customized embed_category: the category lookup calls [0]['id'] unguarded, and since site_settings only stores non-default values, the join returns zero rows and nil['id'] raises, aborting db:migrate
matched_golden_ids: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same root cause: the migration assumes the query returns at least one row and immediately accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without a nil/empty check, causing a crash when embed_category was never customized (no row exists). This matches the golden issue about crashing migrations and breaking category/host relationship editing when no embed_category setting exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration inserts raw setting values via raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalization, so hosts stored with http:// prefixes or paths can never match referers in record_for_host, breaking every previously working embed

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` inserts `embeddable_hosts` setting lines directly via `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, ...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"`, bypassing `EmbeddableHost`’s `before_validation` normalization that strips `http(s)://` and paths. After the change, host checks use `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` which parses the referer URL and compares `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)`. If the old setting contained values like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234` (explicitly shown in updated specs), those would be stored verbatim and would not match `uri.host` (e.g., `discourse.org`), breaking previously allowed embeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Validation permits host:port format but record_for_host compares against uri.host (port excluded), so an admin can save a host like example.com:8080 that never authorizes any embed request

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the validation regex allows an optional `:port` and the `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does not remove the port, so a record can be saved as `example.com:8080` (see `app/models/embeddable_host.rb`). However, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL with `URI(host)` and compares using `uri.host`, which excludes the port, and then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)`. An embed request referer like `http://example.com:8080/...` yields `uri.host == "example.com"`, which will never match the saved DB value `example.com:8080`, causing authorization to fail unexpectedly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin embedding page cannot display existing hosts: the serializer embeds only embeddable_host_ids and Admin::EmbeddingController#show does not side-load embeddable_hosts objects, so the client's _lookupSubType has nothing to resolve and the host table renders empty

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#show` rendering `@embedding` via `render_serialized(@embedding, EmbeddingSerializer, ...)`, and `fetch_embedding` explicitly populates `embeddable_hosts: EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`. The `EmbeddingSerializer` declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, serializer: EmbeddableHostSerializer, embed: :ids`, which in Discourse/AMS is intended to send `embeddable_host_ids` on the parent *and* sideload the associated `embeddable_hosts` records in the same payload. The client-side store was updated to hydrate `*_ids` arrays (see `_hydrateEmbedded` handling `/(.+)_id(s?)$/`), matching that sideloading pattern. The finding's claim that the controller "does not side-load embeddable_hosts objects" is not supported by what is shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy calls host.destroy on a possibly-nil record when the id is stale (already deleted), yielding a 500 instead of a clean response; same pattern in update via save_host(nil)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally operate on it. If the id is stale/missing, `host` will be `nil`, so `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` (NoMethodError) and `destroy` will call `host.destroy` (NoMethodError), yielding a 500 instead of a handled 404/clean response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb and spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb have their contents swapped: category_fabricator.rb contains Fabricator(:embeddable_host) and vice versa, confusing future edits

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` was changed to define `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` (and no longer defines category fabricators), while the newly added `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the category-related fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, etc.). This is a real, diff-grounded maintainability/clarity problem (file names no longer match their contents), but it’s not inherently a functional defect if the test suite loads all fabricators regardless of file name.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead update path: Admin::EmbeddingController#update persists nothing yet a PUT route for customize/embedding exists and the client's saveChanges() calls embedding.update({}), so a future save wired to saveChanges would get a 200 while data is discarded

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a PUT route (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`) and a client action that would invoke it (`saveChanges() { this.get('embedding').update({}); }`), but `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` merely re-renders the current `@embedding` OpenStruct and does not apply or persist any incoming params. This is a real, diff-grounded incompleteness/misleading API surface, but in the current UI (`embedding.hbs`) there is no save button wired to `saveChanges`, and the only actual mutations (adding/updating/deleting hosts) go through `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, so it doesn't presently break behavior or lose user-entered data.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cleanup of embeddable_hosts rows when a category is deleted, so record_for_host keeps returning records whose category_id points at a destroyed category, causing broken or silently recategorized embedded topics in TopicEmbed.import

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces persistent EmbeddableHost rows with a non-null category_id (migration creates embeddable_hosts.category_id null: false) and uses that value to choose the category in TopicEmbed.import (category: eh.try(:category_id)). There is no cleanup/validation shown for when the referenced Category is deleted (EmbeddableHost only has `belongs_to :category` with no dependent/nullify behavior and no FK/cascade shown), and EmbeddableHost.record_for_host/host_allowed? do not check that the associated category still exists. This can leave embeddable_hosts pointing at a destroyed category and then pass a stale category_id into PostCreator, causing incorrect/broken category assignment behavior for newly imported embeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Topic#expandable_first_post? silently dropped its 'hosts configured' guard: the new condition SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed? expands first posts even when all embeddable hosts have been deleted, an unconfirmed behavior change

adjudication.rationale: The diff does verifiably remove the prior “hosts configured” gate in `Topic#expandable_first_post?` (changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` in `app/models/topic.rb`). With this change, if a topic has an embed (`has_topic_embed? == true`) and truncation is enabled, the first post will be expandable regardless of whether any `EmbeddableHost` records exist (even if all hosts have been deleted). However, the diff doesn’t establish that this is incorrect—embedding settings are being migrated from a site setting to the `EmbeddableHost` table—so this looks like a potentially intended behavior change that should be confirmed rather than a clearly provable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: SQL injection risk in migration 20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb: host values from the embeddable_hosts site setting are interpolated directly into an execute INSERT statement with no escaping or parameter binding; a stored host containing a single quote can break the SQL literal, fail the migration, or execute injected SQL (P2)

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"` where `h` comes from the `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts` (split by newlines). Because `h` is inserted into a single-quoted SQL literal without escaping or parameterization, a value containing `'` will break the statement and could allow injected SQL during migration execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:17-20: destroy and update look up EmbeddableHost by id with no nil check; requests with a nonexistent id raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 404 (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code uses `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls methods on the result (`save_host(host)` assigns `host.host = ...`; `host.destroy`). If no record exists for the given id, `host` will be `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 response instead of a 404/not-found handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:11 vs :19: case-sensitivity mismatch — lookup lowercases the DB host but not the incoming host from URI(host).host, and the model never downcases on save, causing legitimate referers with uppercase characters to fail the embed allowlist match (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In EmbeddableHost.record_for_host, the query is `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` but the bound `host` value (from `uri.host`) is not explicitly downcased anywhere in the diff. Since the model’s `before_validation` only strips scheme/path and does not downcase, this creates a case-normalization asymmetry: the left side is forced lowercase while the right side may not be, so a referer/URL with uppercase characters in the hostname could fail to match an allowed host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The new 'find embedded' test requests fruit 2 but the pretender handler always returns fruit 1's payload, so the test asserts canned mock data and never exercises the one-element color_ids hydration path it was changed to cover

adjudication.rationale: In `test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6`, the Pretender handler for `GET /fruits/:id` ignores the requested `:id` and always returns `const fruit = fruits[0];` (apple with `color_ids: [1,2]`). Meanwhile the updated `find embedded` test in `test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6` calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` intending to exercise hydration for a different record (and, per the finding, the one-element `color_ids` case would be fruit 2 = banana with `[3]`). Because the handler always returns fruit 1, the test asserts against canned data and does not actually validate hydration for the requested ID / one-element array path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The pretender handler for GET /fruits/:id ignores the requested :id entirely, always returning fruits[0]

adjudication.rationale: In `test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6`, the Pretender route `this.get('/fruits/:id', function() { const fruit = fruits[0]; ... })` indeed ignores the requested `:id` and always returns the first fruit. However, this is part of the test stub/mocking layer (not production code) and the behavior already existed before this diff (it still used `fruits[0]` previously). It’s a legitimate review concern about test fidelity, but not a newly introduced functional defect in the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embeddable_hosts_controller_spec and embedding_controller_spec contain only class-inheritance tautology assertions and test none of the controllers' actual logic, including save_host's uncategorized category_id fallback and the render_json_error branch

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds two new controller specs (spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb) that only assert the controllers subclass Admin::AdminController. They do not exercise any newly introduced controller behavior such as Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host setting category_id to SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id when blank, nor the error path that calls render_json_error when host.save fails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The embeddable_hosts_controller destroy action does an unguarded host.destroy after a where(id:).first lookup, causing a NoMethodError/500 instead of a 404 for nonexistent ids

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `host.destroy` without checking for `nil` (or using `find`/`find_by!`). If the id doesn’t exist, `host` will be `nil`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 instead of a 404/not_found response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The rewritten 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' test in topic_spec passes vacuously and verifies behavior the code no longer has, since SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? was removed from expandable_first_post?

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb). However, `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` still contains `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` without setting `embed_truncate` true or stubbing `has_topic_embed?`, so it will return false due to the remaining conditions (default `embed_truncate` is false and/or `has_topic_embed?` is false), not due to any "embeddable_host" check. The test is therefore misleading/vacuous and refers to behavior removed by the diff, but this is a test issue rather than a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The sibling 'with an emeddable host' test block in topic_spec uses Fabricate(:embeddable_host) as dead setup, since the production code never reads the embeddable-hosts table on this path

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed to `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (no longer checks `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` and does not reference `EmbeddableHost` at all). Therefore in `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the `describe 'with an emeddable host'` setup `Fabricate(:embeddable_host)` does not affect the behavior under test and is dead/unnecessary setup. This is a test-quality issue, not a production defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Only the matched-host path of EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url) in TopicEmbed.import is covered; the eh == nil branch where category is nil instead of the old SiteSetting.embed_category is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the category is now derived from `eh = EmbeddableHost.record_for_host(url)` and passed as `category: eh.try(:category_id)` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). This introduces an explicit `eh == nil` path where `category` becomes `nil` (no fallback, unlike the previous `SiteSetting.embed_category`). The updated spec only fabricates an `embeddable_host` and asserts the matched-host behavior (`post.topic.category == embeddable_host.category`), and does not cover the `eh == nil` case, so the finding about missing test coverage for that branch is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The rest adapter basePath's new type.replace('_', '-') branch and ADMIN_MODELS addition change URL routing for all REST-backed models with no test coverage, risking silent rerouting to /admin/ (403s) for model types with underscores

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `basePath` to check `ADMIN_MODELS` against `type.replace('_', '-')` and adds only one new admin model (`'embeddable-host'`). This does **not** change routing for “all REST-backed models with underscores”; it only affects types whose underscore-to-dash form matches an entry in `ADMIN_MODELS` (now enabling `embeddable_host` / `site_customization` to correctly map to `/admin/`). The claimed broad risk of silent rerouting/403s for arbitrary underscored models is not supported by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead guard: `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` never passes for SELECT results, so the backfill insert never runs while the paired DELETE still executes, permanently destroying all existing `embeddable_hosts`/`embed_category` settings and breaking external embedding (P0)

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts`, `embeddable_hosts = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")` returns a DB result object (Discourse is Postgres-only). For Postgres `PG::Result#cmd_tuples` on a `SELECT` is the number of rows returned, so `cmd_tuples > 0` will pass when the setting exists and the backfill loop can run. The guard is therefore not "dead" as claimed, and the diff does not show the backfill being skipped while the DELETE always runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unconditional lookup at lines 11-13 dereferences `[0]['id']` without checking rows exist; most sites lack an `embed_category` site_settings row (default is ''), so the migration crashes with NoMethodError and rolls back, blocking deploy (P1)

Irreversible migration: bare `execute` calls in `change` make `down` raise IrreversibleMigration, and the deleted `site_settings` values can never be recovered by dropping the new table; no backup/export step exists (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` defines only a `change` method and includes multiple raw `execute` statements (SELECT/INSERT/DELETE), including `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. With this structure there is no explicit `down` to restore the deleted settings, and Rails cannot infer how to reverse the data moves performed via `execute`, so rolling back would be irreversible / lose the old `site_settings` values. This is a real, diff-grounded concern about rollback/data recovery rather than a runtime functional defect in forward migrations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backfill at lines 27-29 interpolates raw setting values into SQL without parameterization or normalization: single quotes crash the INSERT, and migrated rows containing schemes/paths never match the new `where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host)` lookup so embeds are denied (P2)
matched_golden_ids: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags raw string interpolation of values into an SQL statement “without parameterization,” which is the same underlying problem as the golden comment (lack of binding/quoting leading to SQL injection risk). Although it also mentions correctness issues (single quotes breaking INSERT, normalization mismatches), it still identifies the same core issue of unsafe SQL construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ADVISORY: expand/contract violation for rolling deploys — the migration deletes the settings in the same release that removes the reading code, so old app pods serving during the deploy call `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`/`embed_category` and get blank values, rejecting every embed request until all pods restart

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` copies values out of `site_settings` and then immediately deletes the `embeddable_hosts` and `embed_category` rows (`execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`). In the same PR, the app code removes `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` and stops using `SiteSetting.embed_category`. In a rolling deploy, old pods (still running pre-PR code) would continue to rely on those settings/methods while the migration has already removed the underlying settings values, causing old pods to treat embeddable hosts as unset/invalid and reject embed requests until all pods are updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:11-15 — update/destroy use EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no nil check; a stale/duplicate delete on a missing row yields nil.destroy / save_host(nil) → NoMethodError → raw 500 instead of a 4xx

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without handling the case where no record is found. If the row is missing (stale ID, double-delete, etc.), `host` is `nil`, so `save_host` will raise on `host.host = ...` and `destroy` will raise on `nil.destroy`, causing a 500 instead of a controlled 404/4xx.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:28-29 — save_host dereferences params[:embeddable_host][:host] with no param envelope check, and EmbeddableHost#before_validation calls self.host.sub! on it; a POST/PUT missing the host key raises NoMethodError in the callback → unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx validation error
matched_golden_ids: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate describes the same root bug: EmbeddableHost's before_validation calls `self.host.sub!`, which raises `NoMethodError` when `self.host` is nil (e.g., when the `host` param/key is missing), leading to an unhandled 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:13-15 — EmbeddingController#update accepts a PUT payload and responds with the serialized embedding but persists nothing; clients PUT to the route and get a 200 with unchanged state, making the save path a silent no-op that should not be wired as a writable resource

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a writable route (`put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"`) and an `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` action that ignores params and only re-renders the current `@embedding` (`render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`) without persisting anything. That makes the endpoint semantically misleading (looks like an update but is a no-op). However, the new admin UI template (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) doesn’t call `saveChanges`, and host persistence is handled via `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController`, so this no-op PUT isn’t shown to break any diff-added flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:47-53 — delete() chains destroyRecord().then(...) with no .catch; on DELETE failure the rejection is unhandled and the user sees no error, unlike save() which correctly uses .catch(popupAjaxError)

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6, the delete() action calls this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(...) without any .catch handler. Unlike save(), which ends with .catch(popupAjaxError), a failed DELETE request would result in an unhandled promise rejection and no user-visible error handling in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/embeddable_host.rb:12-22 — record_for_host cannot match hosts the admin UI accepts: the validation regex allows ports and lookup compares uri.host (never includes a port), and the query downcases the stored column but not the uri.host argument, so configured hosts like example.com:8080 or referers like http://Foo.com never match and embed requests get InvalidAccess

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb, before_validation strips scheme/path but leaves an optional port intact (e.g. "example.com:8080" is valid per the regex and will be stored). record_for_host parses the incoming URL with URI() and uses uri.host, which never includes the port, then queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` without downcasing the `host` argument. This means (1) stored hosts with ports will never match referers/URLs ("example.com:8080" stored vs "example.com" looked up), and (2) mixed-case referers like "http://Foo.com" can fail on case-sensitive DBs because `lower(host)` is compared to an undowncased parameter. Since host_allowed? gates embed access, this can cause InvalidAccess for allowed hosts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7 — saveChanges() calls this.get('embedding').update({}) with no .then/.catch and no template binds the action; it's dead code with a fire-and-forget promise pointing at a no-op endpoint and should be removed

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `saveChanges()` in `app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` without any `.then/.catch`, and `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` is effectively a no-op (it just re-renders the serializer without persisting anything). Also, the new `app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/embedding.hbs` does not bind any UI element to the `saveChanges` action (only `addHost` is triggered from the template; per-host saving is handled inside the `embeddable-host` component). This makes `saveChanges` dead/unused code and an unnecessary request path, but not a user-facing functional defect since nothing in the shown diff calls it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/models/store.js.es6:192-200 — the pluralized _hydrateEmbedded branch inserts undefined entries for ids missing from the root collection, and hydrated || [] is a dead fallback since Array.prototype.map never returns falsy; sparse arrays crash or render undefined with no log pointing at the payload mismatch

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded` was changed to handle `*_ids` (plural) via `obj[k].map(...)` and then unconditionally assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and deletes the original `*_ids` key. Since `_lookupSubType(...)` can return a falsy/undefined value (the singular branch explicitly guards `if (hydrated) { ... }`), the plural branch can produce arrays containing `undefined` entries when the root payload lacks some referenced records, while also discarding the original ids. Also, `hydrated || []` is indeed ineffective because `map` always returns an Array. This is a correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Category deletion leaves embeddable_hosts.category_id dangling with no dependent handling or cleanup hook; the client's Discourse.Category.findById(deletedId) returns undefined, the badge silently renders empty, and the next save() commits category_id: nil which the server silently redirects to uncategorized_category_id, silently changing the host's configured category

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces per-host category assignment via `EmbeddableHost` (`belongs_to :category`, `category_id` is required in migration) but adds no dependent handling or referential integrity if a Category is deleted. In the admin component, `edit()` reads `this.get('host.category.id')`; if the category was deleted, `host.category` will be null/undefined, making `categoryId` undefined. On `save()`, it sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` (undefined), and the server controller `save_host` treats blank `category_id` as `uncategorized_category_id`, silently changing the configured category. The UI also renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`, which would be empty when `host.category` is missing.
